Figure 10-24. Valve installed in grinding machine. This image shows a diagram of a valve installed in a grinding machine, illustrating the workhead table, the valve's position for grinding, and the stops that prevent grinding the stem. It highlights the correct adjustment of the valve and the travel adjusted by stops.

Check the travel of the valve face across the stone. The valve should completely pass the stone on both sides, yet not travel far enough to grind the stem. There are stops on the machine that can be set to control this travel.

With the valve set correctly in place, turn on the machine and the grinding fluid so that it splashes on the valve face. Back the grinding wheel off all the way. Place the valve directly in front of the stone. [Figure 10-25] Slowly bring the wheel forward until a light cut is made on the valve. The intensity of the grind is measured by sound more than anything else. Slowly draw the valve back and forth across the stone without increasing the cut. Move the work head table back and forth using the full face of the stone, but always keep the valve face on the stone. When the sound of the grind diminishes, indicating that some valve material has been removed, move the workhead table to the extreme left to stop rotation of the valve. Inspect the valve to determine if further grinding is necessary. If another cut must be made, bring the valve in front of the stone, then advance the stone out to the valve. Do not increase the cut without having the valve directly in front of the stone.

An important precaution in valve grinding, as in any kind of grinding, is to make light cuts only. Heavy cuts cause chattering, that may make the valve surface so rough that much time is lost in obtaining the desired finish.

After grinding, check the valve margin to be sure that the valve edge has not been ground too thin. A thin edge is called a feather edge and can lead to pre-ignition; the valve edge would burn away in a short period of time, and the cylinder would have to be overhauled again. Figure 10-26 shows a valve with a normal margin and one with a feather edge.

The valve tip may be resurfaced on the valve grinder. The tip is ground to remove cupping or wear, and also to adjust valve clearances on some engines.

faqs.question: What should I check if my engine has low rpm and high exhaust gas temperature?
faqs.answer: You should check the inlet pressure line from the probe to the transmitter for leaks and verify the accuracy of the engine pressure ratio transmitter and indicator.

faqs.question: What causes high rpm and high fuel flow in my engine?
faqs.answer: This could be due to a misaligned or cracked turbine discharge probe, a leak in the turbine discharge pressure line, or an inaccurate engine pressure ratio transmitter or indicator.

faqs.question: How can I confirm turbine damage if my engine has high exhaust gas temperature and low rpm?
faqs.answer: You can confirm turbine damage by checking the engine coast-down for abnormal noise and reduced time, and visually inspecting the turbine area with a strong light.

faqs.question: What should I do if my engine vibrates throughout the rpm range?
faqs.answer: You should check the turbine for damage, as this is a common cause of vibration.

faqs.question: What does it mean if my engine vibrates more at cruise or idle rpm?
faqs.answer: This may indicate an issue with an engine-mounted accessory such as a constant-speed drive, generator, or hydraulic pump. You should check each component in turn.

faqs.question: What could be the reason for high oil temperature without changes in power setting parameters?
faqs.answer: The issue may be related to the engine main bearings. You should check the scavenge oil filters and magnetic plugs.

faqs.question: What should I check if my engine has higher than normal exhaust gas temperature during takeoff?
faqs.answer: You should check the operation of the bleed-air valve and the condition of the turbine discharge pressure probe and line to the transmitter.

faqs.question: What does it mean if my engine has high exhaust gas temperature at takeoff pressure ratio?
faqs.answer: This indicates that the engine may be out of trim. You should check the engine with jetcal and re-trim as desired.

faqs.question: What actions should I take if I suspect a leak in the turbine discharge pressure line?
faqs.answer: You should pressure-test the turbine discharge pressure line for leaks and check the engine pressure ratio transmitter and indicator for accuracy.

faqs.question: What are the probable causes of engine vibration at high rpm and fuel flow?
faqs.answer: This could indicate damage in the compressor section, and you should check the compressor section for any damage.

summary.title: Turbojet Engine Troubleshooting Guide
summary.long_summary: This document provides a comprehensive troubleshooting guide for turbojet engines, detailing various malfunctions, their probable causes, and suggested actions to rectify the issues. Key problems include low and high RPMs, abnormal exhaust gas temperatures, and vibrations at different RPM ranges. For instance, low RPM with low exhaust gas temperature and fuel flow may indicate a high reading error in the engine pressure ratio, necessitating checks on the inlet pressure line and the accuracy of the pressure ratio transmitter. Conversely, high RPM with high exhaust gas temperature and fuel flow could suggest misalignment or damage in the turbine discharge probe, requiring inspection and pressure testing of the turbine discharge pressure line. Other issues such as high exhaust gas temperatures during takeoff and climb may point to a malfunctioning bleed-air valve or leaks in the turbine discharge pressure probe line. The guide emphasizes the importance of checking various components, including the turbine and compressor sections, as well as engine-mounted accessories, to ensure optimal engine performance. Additionally, it highlights the need for recalibrating instrumentation when only exhaust gas temperature readings are abnormal. Overall, this troubleshooting guide serves as a valuable resource for diagnosing and addressing common turbojet engine problems.
summary.short_summary: Guide for diagnosing turbojet engine issues.

faqs.question: What should I check if the power unit fails to turn over during an attempted start?
faqs.answer: You should check the starter air valve solenoid and air supply, and unlock the brake by turning the propeller by hand in the direction of normal rotation.

faqs.question: What are the probable causes if the power unit fails to start?
faqs.answer: The probable causes include low starter speed due to inadequate air supply, an inoperative fuel selector valve, a faulty fuel pump, a dirty aircraft fuel filter, or a closed fuel control cutoff valve.

faqs.question: How can I remedy an engine that fires but will not accelerate to the correct speed?
faqs.answer: You should check the fuel system to ensure all valves are open and pumps are operative, flush the system, and replace the control if necessary.

faqs.question: What could cause the acceleration temperature to be too high during starting?
faqs.answer: Possible causes include a stuck open drain valve, a high setting on the starting fuel enrichment pressure switch, a sticking closed fuel control bypass valve, an incorrectly adjusted fuel control acceleration cam, a defective fuel nozzle, or a fuel control thermostat failure.

faqs.question: What should I do if the acceleration temperature during starting is too low?
faqs.answer: You should replace the fuel control.

faqs.question: What does it mean if the engine speed cycles after starting?
faqs.answer: This indicates unstable fuel control governor operation, and you should continue engine operation to allow the control to condition itself.

faqs.question: What could cause the power unit oil pressure to drop off severely?
faqs.answer: The causes could be low oil supply or a false indication from the oil pressure transmitter or indicator.

faqs.question: What should I do if there is oil leakage at the accessory drive seals?
faqs.answer: You need to replace the seal or seals.

faqs.question: What might prevent the engine from reaching the maximum controlled speed of 100 percent?
faqs.answer: This could be due to a faulty propeller governor or a faulty fuel control or air sensing tip.

faqs.question: What actions should I take if the vibration indication is high?
faqs.answer: You should calibrate the vibration meter, start the engine and gradually increase power, and observe the vibration indicator. If the pickup is at fault, replace it; if high vibration remains, remove the power unit for overhaul.

summary.title: Troubleshooting Guide for Turboprop Engines
summary.long_summary: This document provides a troubleshooting guide for turboprop engines, outlining common issues, their probable causes, and recommended remedies. Key problems include the power unit failing to turn over, start, or accelerate properly, as well as issues with oil pressure and vibration. For instance, if the power unit fails to turn over, it may be due to a lack of air to the starter or a locked propeller brake. Remedies involve checking the starter air valve solenoid and unlocking the brake. If the power unit fails to start, potential causes include low starter speed due to inadequate air supply, an inoperative fuel selector valve, or a dirty fuel filter. Suggested actions include checking the air supply, inspecting electrical circuits, and cleaning or replacing filters. Other issues addressed include engine acceleration problems, temperature fluctuations during starting, oil pressure drops, and high vibration indications. Each problem is paired with specific checks and replacements to ensure proper engine function. This guide serves as a comprehensive resource for diagnosing and resolving turboprop engine issues effectively.
summary.short_summary: Common issues and remedies for turboprop engines.

faqs.question: What should I do if my engine is running unevenly and has low power?
faqs.answer: Check for restrictions in the exhaust system and verify the ignition timing. Remove any restrictions and check the magnetos for timing and synchronization.

faqs.question: Why is my engine not developing full power?
faqs.answer: This could be due to an improperly adjusted throttle lever or a leak in the induction system. Adjust the throttle lever and tighten all connections, replacing any defective parts.

faqs.question: What causes a rough running engine?
faqs.answer: Possible causes include cracked engine mounts, an unbalanced propeller, defective mounting bushings, lead deposits on spark plugs, or an unlocked primer. Repair or replace the mounts, check the propeller balance, install new bushings, clean or replace the plugs, and lock the primer.

faqs.question: How can I fix low oil pressure?
faqs.answer: Check the oil supply, clean the oil strainers, replace the pressure gauge, and remove any dirt from the oil pressure relief valve. Also, check for leaks in the suction or pressure lines.

faqs.question: What are the remedies for high oil temperature?
faqs.answer: Overhaul the engine and check the air inlet and outlet for any deformation or obstruction. Ensure there is sufficient oil supply and clean any clogged oil lines or strainers.

faqs.question: What should I do if I experience excessive oil consumption?
faqs.answer: Check for failing bearings, worn or broken piston rings, incorrect installation of piston rings, or external oil leakage. Install new rings and check for leaking gaskets or O-rings.

faqs.question: What could cause my engine to have a leak in the oil lines?
faqs.answer: Leaks can occur due to insufficient oil supply, clogged oil lines or strainers, or failing bearings. Ensure the oil tank is filled to the proper level and clean any clogged lines or strainers.

faqs.question: How do I address a defective temperature gauge?
faqs.answer: Replace the defective temperature gauge and check for any other issues that may be causing high oil temperature, such as worn bearings or insufficient air cooling.

faqs.question: What should I check if my engine has a leak through the fuel pump vent?
faqs.answer: Replace the fuel pump seal and check the engine. If necessary, overhaul or replace the vacuum pump.

faqs.question: What are the signs of a cracked engine mount?
faqs.answer: A rough running engine can indicate cracked engine mounts. Inspect the mounts for any visible cracks or damage.

summary.title: Troubleshooting Guide for Opposed Engines
summary.long_summary: This document provides a comprehensive troubleshooting guide for opposed engines, detailing common issues, probable causes, and recommended remedies. Key problems include low power and uneven engine running, which may arise from restrictions in the exhaust system or improper ignition timing. Remedies involve removing restrictions and checking magnetos for timing and synchronization. Another issue is the engine failing to develop full power, often due to throttle lever misadjustment or leaks in the induction system, which can be resolved by adjusting the throttle lever and tightening connections. Additional causes for power loss include restrictions in the carburetor airscoop, improper fuel, and faulty ignition, with remedies such as examining the airscoop, using recommended fuel, and checking ignition timing. Rough running engines may result from cracked engine mounts or unbalanced propellers, necessitating repairs or replacements. Low oil pressure can stem from insufficient oil, dirty strainers, or leaks, with solutions including checking oil supply and cleaning strainers. High oil temperature issues may arise from worn bearings or insufficient cooling, requiring engine overhauls and checks for obstructions. Excessive oil consumption can indicate failing bearings or worn piston rings, with remedies including installing new rings and checking for external leaks. This guide serves as a valuable resource for diagnosing and addressing engine problems effectively.
